item.title: 029 美国华人移民自闭症儿童家庭的沉默政治与父母抗争 Advocacy of Autistic Parents
item.description:
【聊了什么】

这一期是纽约文化沙龙线下活动的录音。我们从最基础的问题开始聊：自闭症到底是什么，为什么早诊断这么关键，为什么华裔家庭的诊断普遍偏晚。然后一路聊到更艰难的部分：神经多样性和残障权利框架之间的张力，高功能/低功能这套话语为什么害人，profound autism 这个新定义在争什么，ABA 到底该怎么看，以及所有家长最怕被问到的那个问题——我们老了、走了以后，孩子怎么办？

This episode is a recording of an in-person New York Culture Salon event. We start with the most basic questions: what autism actually is, why early diagnosis matters so much, and why diagnosis tends to come late in Chinese American families. From there we move into harder territory — the tension between the neurodiversity framework and the disability rights framework, why the high-functioning/low-functioning vocabulary does real damage, what's at stake in the new "profound autism" definition, how to think about ABA, and the question every parent dreads: what happens to our child after we grow old and are gone?

item.title: 028 硅谷遇上教宗通谕：谁有权力重新定义“人” Pope Leo XIV's AI Encyclical
item.description:
【聊了什么】

当下的硅谷正流行着一种“技术拯救主义”，试图通过AI实现意识上传、星际殖民，甚至彻底消灭死亡。在教宗良十四看来，这不过是披着科技外衣的古老诱惑。本期节目围绕最新通谕，展开了一场关于人论的思辨。我们探讨为什么“有限性”并非人性的缺陷、反而是成圣的阶梯，抨击了将人指标化、工具化的“被动式人文主义”。当AI开始模拟情感与直觉，人的边界在哪里？硅谷盛行的TESCREAL意识形态，为何被视为现代版的“巴别塔”？面对AI带来的功能性取代，宗教人本主义如何通过本体论捍卫人类尊严？

A kind of "techno-salvationism" is in vogue in Silicon Valley right now — the attempt to use AI to achieve mind uploading, interstellar colonization, even the total abolition of death. In the eyes of Pope Leo XIV, this is nothing but an ancient temptation dressed in technological clothing. This episode takes the latest encyclical as its starting point for a philosophical inquiry into the nature of the human person. We explore why "finitude" is not a defect in human nature but rather a ladder toward sanctification, and we take aim at the "passive humanism" that reduces people to metrics and instruments. As AI begins to simulate emotion and intuition, where does the boundary of the human lie? Why is the TESCREAL ideology so prevalent in Silicon Valley seen as a modern Tower of Babel? In the face of the functional replacement AI brings, how does religious humanism defend human dignity by way of ontology?

海德格尔在 1938 年说过一句话：世界进入了一个"图像化的时代"——它不再和我们一起存在，而是变成了一个被观察、被研究、被掌握的对象。

这期是《选修课》在狂喜播客节攒的一个四方连线，每人填一个半命题：世界是一个 ______。

物理学家老赵填的是钟表，传播学者方可成填的是洞穴，残障研究者仁慈填的是巨大的楼梯，律师 Lokin 填的是草台班子。

四张图像并置起来，照见了现代性的一些隐秘脉络——为什么我们这么依赖量化？为什么"客观"成了一个越来越站不住脚的承诺？神死之后我们靠什么获得确定性？以及，AI 时代，我们是该悲观还是乐观？

In 1938, Heidegger wrote that the world had entered "the age of the world picture" — no longer something we inhabit alongside, but something to be observed, st…In 1938, Heidegger wrote that the world had entered "the age of the world picture" — no longer something we inhabit alongside, but something to be observed, studied, and mastered as an object.

This episode is a four-way crossover recorded for the Kuangxi Podcast Festival, hosted by Elective Course. Each guest was asked to fill in a blank: The world is a ______.

Physicist Lao Zhao filled in a clockwork. Communications scholar Fang Kecheng filled in a cave. Disability studies scholar Mercy filled in a giant staircase. Lawyer Lokin filled in a slapdash operation.

Placed side by side, the four images expose some of the hidden grain of modernity — why we've grown so dependent on quantification, why "objectivity" has become an increasingly untenable promise, what we turn to for certainty after the death of God, and whether, in the age of AI, we should be pessimistic or optimistic.

item.description:

本期节目邀请到前 Meta 人工智能研究院高级经理田渊栋，与哥伦比亚大学商学院助理教授彭天翼，共同探讨 2026 年 AI 的核心命题：个性化。从冯·诺依曼架构的‘存算分离’到大模型的‘存算一体’，我们深入拆解了 AI 如何通过显性与隐性记忆构建个人数字孪生。我们还特别针对学术界与工业界的‘地位倒挂’、端侧 AI 的隐私平衡以及 AI for Science 等热门话题进行了全方位碰撞。当下的 AI 究竟是通才工具，还是具备独特审美与思维方式的个人助理？在 AI 时代，人类如何通过提出‘宏大愿景’来定义自我价值？

In this episode, we are joined by Yuandong Tian, former Senior Manager at Meta AI Research, and Tianyi Peng, Assistant Professor at Columbia Business School, for a wide-ranging conversation on one of the defining questions of AI in 2026: personalization.

From the “separation of memory and computation” in the von Neumann architecture to the emerging “fusion of memory and computation” in large models, we unpack how AI may build a personal digital twin through both explicit and implicit forms of memory. 谎言，是人类社会的润滑剂，还是效率的绊脚石？是一种自我保护的自由，还是滋生不公的温床？当「我没问题」「收到」「您说得对」背后真实的吐槽被强制公之于众，你的职场生活会更好还是更坏呢？《选修课》「如果宇宙」思想实验系列，再次撕开现实的口子，邀请你一同推想一个“无谎职场”。

我们探讨了当“防御性谎言”和“心照不宣的潜规则”消失后，一系列连锁反应将如何展开：预算博弈的“囚徒困境”能否被终结？等级森严的组织中，是会催生出更强的个体，还是会强迫人们将“崇拜”内化为真实信仰？从语言学的角度看，当隐喻与模糊性被视为不诚实，我们的沟通能力是否会被根本性地剥夺？00后新人为何期盼一个没有潜规则的世界？而体制内的“防御性表演”又将在绝对诚实面前何去何从？当情绪价值被重新估量，当“演戏”不再可能，我们究竟离一个更好的职场更近了，还是更远了？

Are lies the lubricant of human society or the stumbling block of efficiency? Are they a form of self-protection and personal freedom, or the breeding ground of injustice? When everyday workplace phrases like “I’m fine,” “Got it,” and “You’re right” are forced to give way to the truth behind the polite facades, will your work life become better—or worse?

In this episode of Elective Course's “What If Universe” thought experiment series, we once again tear open a crack in reality and invite you to imagine a world with no lies at work.

We explore the chain reactions that could follow the disappearance of "defensive lies" and unspoken workplace rules:Can the budgetary “prisoner’s dilemma” be resolved? In rigid hierarchies, will this honesty foster stronger individuals—or compel people to internalize flattery as genuine belief?

From a linguistic standpoint, if metaphors and ambiguity are deemed dishonest, are we fundamentally robbed of our ability to communicate? Why do Gen Z newcomers long for a workplace without unspoken rules? And in the bureaucracy, what happens to “defensive performances” when absolute honesty becomes the norm?
